metadata.label: Shape model
metadata.coverage: Published PDS shape model, including poorly constrained source estimates. Both views use the gray grid for source-flagged poorly constrained regions. Source constraints keeps solid gray for stereo control and blue for limb silhouettes. Grid regions lack those constraints; they are not necessarily wholly unobserved. These are evidence categories, not surface colors. The cartographic north direction follows the long axis at the 2010 encounter, not a spin pole. Hartley 2 tumbles; this display holds an arbitrary rotational phase and does not simulate that motion.

metadata.label: EPOXI photographs
metadata.coverage: MRI and restored HRI photographs from the EPOXI flyby are combined on the nucleus. HRI supplies finer image sampling, with MRI extending the coverage. Original shadows remain; the gray grid marks gaps or poorly constrained shape.

celestial.sunSource: JPL Horizons osculating elements; PDS source orientation held at arbitrary phase.

controls.label: Source constraints
controls.notes: Shape measurements mapped onto the nucleus. Solid gray marks stereo measurements, blue marks limb outlines, and the grid marks poorly constrained regions.

controls.label: Shape model
controls.notes: The published nucleus shape, simplified for display. Gray is a model material; the grid marks regions with weaker shape constraints.

controls.label: EPOXI photographs
controls.notes: EPOXI photographed Hartley’s smooth waist and rough lobes during its 2010 flyby. This mosaic combines MRI views with HRI images restored by the mission team. Original shadows and some restoration grain remain; the grid marks gaps or uncertain shape.

controls.label: Color temperature
controls.notes: False colors show the temperature fitted to infrared emission. Warm patches within each pixel dominate this measurement. Placement on the shape is approximate; the grid marks gaps.

controls.label: Infrared slope
controls.notes: False colors show how quickly reflected sunlight becomes brighter toward longer infrared wavelengths. Higher values mean a redder spectrum. Placement on the shape is approximate; the grid marks gaps. This does not measure terrain slope or identify minerals.
